reasons.A: Modern, even-paced and confiding ('I think', 'It seems to me'), with contemporary diction; it lacks the passage's abrupt short sentences, compressed irony and period register.
reasons.B: Period diction and double-dash asides fit, but it runs as long, evenly balanced periodic sentences in two big blocks, missing the passage's clipped declaratives and sudden turns; 'I know not when' pushes towards pastiche.
reasons.C: Closest movement: short blunt declaratives set against longer clauses, dry assertive irony ('Surely it is the other way'), period touches like 'learnt' and double-dash asides, and a terse epigrammatic close, all without laying the mannerisms on too thick.
